headline: The +94% volume block delivered a genuine easy-run efficiency gain: comparable-effort HR is running roughly 9 beats lower.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days
confidence_attention: Limited data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The story of this block is efficiency, and it's now holding across enough runs to trust. Saturday's 20 km sat comfortably in the low aerobic band at a controlled effort, and the same pattern shows up across the recent easy work — you're moving at familiar paces for noticeably less cardiac cost than the prior period. This is the answer to the question left open last week: the lower HR band has held even as volume climbed, so it reads as a real adaptation rather than a recovery-week artefact.

What's less clear-cut is the intensity distribution. Almost everything recently has lived in Z1–Z2, with only a token amount of time above threshold. That's appropriate given the volume ramp and the pilgrim crossing on the horizon — this is base-building that plays directly to the 580 km demand. But the efficiency signal was earned on easy running; you haven't yet stress-tested whether it survives a genuinely hard effort. Don't read the "detraining" strain label as fitness loss — it reflects Polar's rolling comparison against a heavier 28-day window and sits alongside your highest volume block, so the two contradict each other and the volume is the more reliable signal.

Strength has been the quiet anchor here — three times the session count of the prior block, sustained right through the volume ramp. That's a meaningful piece of the hybrid picture holding steady while running load builds.
watch_items: Whether the lower easy-run HR band holds the first time a genuinely hard or threshold session returns.
Whether loaded pack-carry running and sustained (not just rolling) climbing enter the schedule with enough runway before the crossing.
Whether weekly Z2 minutes climb back toward the intended range as the base block continues, given how little time has sat above easy lately.
Whether the short-night cluster settles back toward the block average or stretches further.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 181 km vs 94 km prior block (+94%)
▼ Strain:tolerance ratio 0.18 (DETRAINING) (strain 11, tolerance 59); sleep averaging 7h10m over the same period
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 142 bpm vs 151 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 10 vs 5 runs)
